elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the report as an integrative review, not explicitly as a systematic review.

elements.quote: we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review objective.

elements.quote: Included studies were not restricted by research design; and had to evaluate the sustainability of an EBI in a healthcare context.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria are specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: a comprehensive search strategy was applied across five databases
elements.reason: Information sources (five databases) are mentioned, but the abstract does not state when each source was last searched.

elements.quote: We assessed the methodological quality of studies using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.
elements.reason: Risk of bias/methodological quality assessment method is named in the abstract.

elements.quote: Following Whittemore and Knafl's methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis; and (5) presentation
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used for data analysis/synthesis and presentation of results.

elements.quote: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria. Qualitative designs were most commonly used for evaluation (48%), with individual interviews as the predominant data collection method.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and summarizes relevant study characteristics.

elements.quote: Of the 64 studies, 44% used a framework, 26% used a model, 11% used a tool, 5% used an instrument, and 14% used theory as their primary approach to evaluate sustainability. Most studies (77%) did not measure sustainability outcomes
elements.reason: The abstract presents main results with numbers of studies for each finding.
No meta-analysis was conducted; this is a narrative synthesis integrative review.
No group comparisons with effect estimates are reported; the review synthesizes approaches descriptively.
The abstract does not summarize limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias or incompleteness; the Discussion sentence addresses field-level gaps, not evidence limitations.

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation and implications of the results.
The abstract does not mention any funding source for the review.
The abstract does not report a registration name or registration number.

elements.quote: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement.
elements.reason: The background describes the current state of knowledge (limited evidence on sustainability evaluation, 17-year translation lag, maturing implementation science) and identifies the uncertainty that it is unclear which approaches are most effective.

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used... Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained: the gap in guidance on selecting approaches to evaluate sustainability and the aim to advance the field.

elements.quote: A focus on evaluation is what differentiates this review from recent syntheses published on approaches to sustainability research.
elements.reason: The manuscript acknowledges similar recent syntheses (citing [6-10], e.g., Lennox et al.) and explains how the current review differs by focusing on evaluation approaches, timing, methods, measures, and outcomes.
This is a review of approaches used to evaluate sustainability of EBIs, not a review of intervention effects, so describing a mechanism of action of an intervention does not apply.
The review examines evaluation approaches rather than assessing a specific complex intervention's components and outcomes, so a logic model requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare. We aimed to enhance our understanding of sustainability definitions, research designs, data collection methods, timing, measures, and sustainability outcomes used for sustainability evaluation studies.
elements.reason: The review objectives are explicitly stated in a dedicated Aim section, also echoed in the abstract.

elements.quote: Integrative reviews can include diverse data sources and do not restrict the type of study design.
elements.reason: This is an integrative review of approaches to evaluating sustainability, not a review of intervention effects, so PICO-style planned comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal • Were primary research • Had explicit research design and data collection methods • Had an explicit theoretical approach for sustainability ... • Were within a healthcare setting • Evaluated the sustainability of an EBI
elements.reason: Table 1 specifies study characteristics for eligibility: study design (primary research with explicit design/methods), setting (healthcare, with definition in footnote g), and requirement of an explicit theoretical approach and independent sustainability evaluation component.

elements.quote: • Were published in a peer-review journal ... Articles were excluded if they: • Were secondary research • Were gray literature
elements.reason: Publication status is specified (peer-reviewed primary research; gray literature excluded), but dissemination year and language restrictions are not stated in the eligibility criteria; the English-language restriction appears only in the Limitations section (text_21), not as an eligibility criterion.
The review addresses sustainability outcomes, but nowhere distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

No evidence specifies groups used in each synthesis or links them to review comparisons; the review descriptively categorizes approaches (framework, model, tool, instrument, theory) in results but no grouping for syntheses is defined in the methods.

Notable restrictions (e.g., healthcare settings only, independent sustainability evaluation component required, peer-reviewed publications only) are stated but no rationales for these restrictions are provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: In December 2018 and July 2020, we searched the following databases: Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process and Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current).
elements.reason: Search dates for all sources are reported (December 2018 and July 2020), with the supplementary file specifying 'The four databases searched on Dec 21, 2018, as well as an additional search in July 2020' (text_24).

elements.quote: Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process and Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current).
elements.reason: Each database is named with its platform/interface (Ovid, EBSCOhost, Wiley) and coverage dates (e.g., 1946 to current, 1974 to current).

elements.quote: We extracted whether an included study evaluated (a) sustainability determinants and (b) sustainability outcomes and how they measured these variables. We defined sustainability determinants as correlates and predictors of sustainability (organizational, contextual, and strategies) and sustainability outcomes as the subsequent impact (healthcare improvement or public health outcomes) of sustained intervention use [5]. To further unpack sustainability outcomes, we extracted and synthesized nine sustainability outcomes across the 64 included studies (Table 3)
elements.reason: Two broad outcome domains (determinants and outcomes) are defined, and nine sustainability outcomes are listed (text_15, Table 3), but the nine outcomes are not individually defined in the methods.

elements.quote: (7) timing of evaluation data collection (e.g., pre-, and/or post-implementation of intervention)

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite), (3) sustainability definition and terms used, (4) type and name of theoretical approach, (5) purpose of approach use, (6) data collection methods, (7) timing of evaluation data collection (e.g., pre-, and/or post-implementation of intervention), (8) reported sustainability measures and, 9. reported sustainability outcomes.

elements.reason: The tool (MMAT) is explicitly named.

elements.quote: Each study is assigned an overall quality score, using asterisks representing the quality appraisal of each study. Scores vary from 20% (*) when one criterion is met to 100% (*****) when all criteria are met.
elements.reason: Overall judgement (score) and rules for deriving it are reported.

elements.quote: After removing duplicates, we conducted a two-stage screening process of the citations retrieved from our database searches... In the second stage, two reviewers (RF and AB) independently screened all full-text articles that had passed first-stage screening. We discussed any differences in screening at team meetings and refined our inclusion and exclusion criteria to reflect these discussions.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the general eligibility screening process (two-stage screening, independent reviewers, refinement of inclusion/exclusion criteria), but does not describe processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis (e.g., tabulating study characteristics against planned synthesis groups). The synthesis grouping is only briefly noted in text_12 ('We compared, grouped, and synthesized each study by these variables'), without explaining how eligibility for each synthesis was determined.

The methods describe screening, extraction variables, and the Whittemore and Knafl analysis stages (data reduction, display, comparison), but no methods for preparing data for presentation or synthesis—such as handling missing summary statistics or data conversions—are reported.

elements.quote: Data analysis followed the methodological steps outlined by Whittemore and Knafl [12] which included data reduction, data display, data comparison, and drawing conclusions and verifications. We compared, grouped, and synthesized each study by these variables. Evidence tables were created to summarize and describe the studies included in this review.
